evidence: (a) Whole-artifact search found no equivalent source-eligibility, service-session exclusion, or finite stopping rule. CURRENT-DESIGN.md:32-34 says graph detects transcript work, activates the ordinary summarizer seat, and its occupant dispatches subagents; DESIGN-NOTES.md:241,247-258 adds closure-triggered requests and durable completion but leaves detection/identity details open. (b) Accepted tradeoffs put dispatch in role instructions and omit periodic model wakes or a plugin worker pool (DESIGN-NOTES.md:248-250); none decides which closed transcripts create new requests. (c) A bounded eligibility policy fits the approved transcript workflow and does not demand a new worker architecture. (d) If summarizer/helper sessions qualify, processing can create further eligible sessions and repeatedly reactivate the seat after user work ends, conflicting with useful dormancy in HERDR-GRAPH-VISION.md, Principles to preserve. This is a material conditional design gap, not a claim that recursion is inevitable or currently implemented. No external premise is needed.
